briefs.source_chain: Post-Muse return of the +Semis/-AI Vulnerable trade drives a Financials selloff (XLF -2%) against an AI/semis rally (SOXX +2.4%, DRAM +3.3%) therefore O'Dwyer argues the bank-funding-risk narrative doesn't hold (Muse itself untrustworthy) and reads consensus-name-led volume (C/MS/GS/USB) vs regional/LAZ/JEF outperformance as a positioning unwind, so he fades the selloff favoring MS/PNC/FITB; separately Adler frames Muse as agents succeeding chatbots, favoring META/GOOGL/AAPL on trust (with a noted caveat that agents could hurt GOOGL's own search business), easing reliance on frontier chips (a neocloud headwind) and diversifying the AI trade toward CPU/memory/storage/networking away from GPUs, while turning cautious on frontier-model economics near RSI; oil fell 1.2% despite Iran's conditional Strait offer and Rubio's flow comment because Trump again pushed a deal past the midterms; Fedspeak (Barkin plus the hawkish Fri/Sun echo of Warsh) raises hike risk; JPM stays Tactically Cautious/Neutral, would only turn bullish on lower oil/yields, and keeps +Tech/-RTY plus a Latam long.

briefs.source_chain: Warsh's late-August Jackson Hole hawkishness plus broadening survey inflation had already shifted rate expectations before Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and reported Hormuz shipping disruption pushed Brent above $100, feeding gasoline-driven CPI/PPI upside and cited by the BoE as an upward risk, therefore the FOMC hiked 25bp unanimously to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sept with Warsh signaling more tightening; the S&P sold off >1% intraday then recovered as yields/oil eased and flows rotated back to AI tech; a year of earnings outpacing price gains had already compressed forward P/E from ~23x (Oct 2025) to 19.1x, cushioning the hike; the BoJ hiked 25bp to a 31-year high of 1.25% yet the yen weakened past 156 as the widening Fed-BoJ gap and a split BoJ vote kept carry trades intact; the bank holds a neutral equity stance, weighing constructive earnings against higher real-rate risk.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same order and same causal links: Jackson Hole hawkishness and broadening inflation predate the oil shock (Houthi attacks, Hormuz disruption, Brent >$100, CPI/PPI upside, BoE citation) therefore the Fed's unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% with more tightening signaled; S&P sold off >1% intraday then recovered on easing yields/oil and AI-tech rotation; P/E compression from ~23x to 19.1x left room to absorb the hike; BoJ hiked 25bp to a 31-year high of 1.25% while the yen weakened past 156 on the Fed-BoJ gap and split vote; bank stays neutral on equities, constructive earnings vs. higher real-rate risk.
